Nvidia / skip - Lattice Semiconductor.role: Lattice makes small, low-power FPGAs for edge/industrial/comms applications; it is cyclically exposed to inventory corrections and holds a #2 niche position rather than a dominant moat, so its AI-edge story is real but modest and not yet a durable growth driver.

Microchip Technology.role: Broad-line supplier of microcontrollers and analog/embedded chips increasingly used for edge AI inference in industrial, automotive, and IoT; it sits as cyclical AI-infra because demand is real and recurring but highly tied to inventory cycles and discretionary capex, limiting its direct AI-growth l

Analog Devices.role: ADI is a diversified high-performance analog/mixed-signal supplier whose power and signal-chain content is rising in data-center and AI infrastructure; it sits as durable AI-infra but with cyclical industrial/auto exposure that tempers pure AI leverage.

NXP Semiconductors.role: NXP is a leading automotive and industrial semiconductor supplier whose edge-processing, radar, and microcontroller franchises anchor it to car electrification and ADAS; it sits in AI-infra as a cyclical, moderately durable play exposed to auto-production swings rather than hyperscaler capex.

ON Semiconductor.role: ON is a power/analog semiconductor maker with strong auto/industrial exposure and an emerging datacenter power-delivery angle for AI; it sits in AI-infra but with modest AI revenue share, cyclical end-markets, and auto/industrial softness pressuring near-term growth.

GlobalFoundries.role: GlobalFoundries is a specialty semiconductor foundry focused on mature/differentiated process nodes (RF, auto, IoT, power) rather than leading-edge AI logic; it sits in AI-infra but with modest growth, cyclical end-markets, and limited moat versus TSMC, making its AI exposure indirect and its earnin

Entegris.role: Entegris supplies ultra-high-purity materials, filtration, and advanced handling solutions consumed in chip fabrication; its consumable-heavy revenue base ties it to wafer starts and leading-edge node transitions, giving it recurring exposure with moderate cyclicality rather than pure capex risk.

MKS Instruments.role: MKS supplies subsystems and process control instruments (vacuum, lasers, RF power, optics) used in semiconductor fabrication and advanced packaging; it sits in AI-infra as a cyclical, capex-levered supplier with solid niche moats but heavy exposure to wafer-fab equipment spending swings and a signif

Axcelis Technologies.role: Supplier of ion implantation systems for semiconductor fabrication, strong in power/mature-node (SiC, automotive) rather than leading-edge AI logic, making it a cyclical WFE name exposed to capex swings and the current power-chip downcycle.

Photronics.role: Leading independent maker of photomasks used in chip and flat-panel lithography; a credible merchant-market duopolist with real customer demand but modest growth and cyclicality tied to semiconductor capex.

FormFactor.role: Leading supplier of advanced probe cards and test systems used in semiconductor wafer testing; benefits from AI/HBM chip complexity but revenue is tied to cyclical fab test capex and foundry utilization.

Cirrus Logic.role: Fabless mixed-signal and audio chip supplier heavily concentrated in Apple smartphones; modest growth and customer-concentration risk place it as a cyclical, mid-quality edge-silicon name rather than a core AI-infra beneficiary.

Power Integrations.role: Power Integrations designs high-voltage power-conversion semiconductors used in chargers, appliances, industrial and increasingly data-center/AI power delivery; it sits in AI-infra with moderate growth as a cyclical-but-quality analog supplier with solid niche moats but exposure to consumer/industri

Allegro MicroSystems.role: Allegro makes Hall-effect magnetic sensors and power ICs mostly for automotive (EV/ADAS) and industrial markets; it sits as a cyclical semiconductor name with solid niche share but exposure to auto/industrial demand swings rather than secular AI data-center growth.

Diodes Incorporated.role: Diodes makes commodity discrete and analog semiconductors for consumer, industrial, and automotive end-markets; broad-line but fragmented and cyclical, with only indirect AI exposure, so it sits as a cyclical semiconductor name rather than a core AI-infra play.

MACOM Technology.role: MACOM supplies analog RF, microwave, and high-speed optical/photonic components for data-center, telecom, and defense networking; it benefits from AI-driven optical connectivity demand but competes in a fragmented analog market with cyclical and defense-tied revenue streams.

Qorvo.role: Qorvo makes RF front-end components concentrated in mobile handsets (Apple/Android exposure), a cyclical, customer-concentrated business with modest growth and limited direct AI leverage, placing it as a mid-quality cyclical semi name.

Skyworks Solutions.role: Supplier of RF front-end modules and filters for smartphones and IoT; heavy Apple concentration and smartphone cyclicality cap growth, placing it as a mature, modestly-valued cyclical rather than an AI-infra beneficiary.

Synopsys.role: Synopsys is a dominant EDA vendor whose design and verification tools are mission-critical, recurring software embedded in every advanced chip workflow, giving durable demand that largely survives capex cycles.

Cadence Design Systems.role: Cadence is a dominant EDA vendor in a tight duopoly with Synopsys, providing mission-critical chip design software with recurring revenue that is largely non-discretionary for semiconductor customers, giving it a durable moat and resilience through capex cycles.

Synaptics.role: Supplies human-interface and connectivity chips plus edge-AI IoT processors; mid-tier semiconductor name with cyclical consumer exposure and a credible but unproven edge-AI growth narrative, placing it in moderate-moat, cyclical territory.

Aehr Test Systems.role: Aehr makes wafer-level burn-in and test systems historically tied to SiC/EV power devices now pivoting toward AI/HPC processor test; it is a small, cyclical, customer-concentrated equipment supplier whose demand swings with capex cycles, hence high beta and modest capex elasticity.

UiPath.role: UiPath is a leading enterprise RPA and agentic automation platform with recurring subscription revenue, but faces slowing growth, intense competition from Microsoft and AI-native entrants, and discretionary IT spend exposure that caps its moat and durability.

Salesforce.role: Dominant SaaS CRM vendor layering Agentforce AI agents atop recurring enterprise subscriptions; sticky installed base and strong cash flow make it durable, but mature low-teens growth and uncertain AI monetization cap upside.

Twilio.role: Twilio provides programmable messaging, voice, and customer-data APIs now layering AI/contextual communications; mid-single-moat with usage-based recurring revenue but exposed to developer/marketing spend cyclicality and intense CPaaS competition.

Fortinet.role: Fortinet sells firewalls and an integrated security fabric with recurring subscription revenue; durable demand and strong profitability place it as a defensive, moderate-growth cybersecurity incumbent rather than a speculative AI name.

Palo Alto Networks.role: Leading next-gen cybersecurity vendor consolidating network, cloud, and SecOps into an AI-infused platform; recurring subscription revenue and non-discretionary security spend give durable, defensible growth, placing it as a quality AI-platform name rather than a speculative play.

Okta.role: Okta provides cloud-based identity and access management with recurring subscription revenue; it sits as a quality mid-tier software name with durable demand but faces stiff competition from Microsoft Entra, capping dominance and growth.

DigitalOcean.role: Developer-friendly cloud provider serving SMBs and startups with a nascent GPU/AI offering (post-Paperspace), but it competes against hyperscalers from a subscale position with modest moat and uneven AI traction.

Pure Storage.role: All-flash enterprise storage vendor benefiting from AI data pipeline and hyperscaler deals; solid profitability and recurring subscription mix but competes against larger incumbents (Dell, NetApp) in a cyclical hardware market.

NetApp.role: NetApp is a mature hybrid-cloud data storage vendor positioning its all-flash and intelligent data infrastructure for enterprise AI workloads; it sits defensively given stable recurring revenue, modest growth, and a competitive but non-dominant position in a fragmented storage market.

Equinix.role: Leading colocation and interconnection REIT whose recurring, contracted revenue and network-dense facilities make it a durable AI-infra beneficiary, though its REIT structure, high capital intensity, and moderate growth cap its upside versus pure-play compute names.

Digital Realty Trust.role: Digital Realty is a leading global data center REIT leasing colocation and hyperscale capacity that underpins AI/cloud buildouts; durable recurring rental income and interconnection moats sit it in AI-infra with modest growth and defensive-leaning risk, though high valuation (REIT FFO multiple) and

Iron Mountain.role: Legacy records-storage REIT pivoting into data center colocation; durable recurring cash flows and sticky customers anchor a credible but still-emerging AI-infra growth leg, placing it between defensive and infra.

Constellation Energy.role: Largest U.S. nuclear fleet operator supplying carbon-free baseload power increasingly contracted to hyperscaler data centers; durable regulated-style cash flows and essential demand place it in defensive despite AI-driven upside, though valuation already reflects substantial nuclear-AI optimism.

Vistra.role: Vistra is an independent power producer with nuclear and gas assets positioned to supply surging datacenter demand; it sits in defensive-infra with durable recurring power revenue but cyclical commodity exposure and modest moat in a regulated, competitive market.

GE Vernova.role: Leading supplier of grid, gas, and electrification equipment riding datacenter-driven power demand; sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels beneficiary with solid backlog but exposure to utility capex cycles.

Quanta Services.role: Leading specialty contractor for electric power transmission, distribution, and grid modernization; benefits from data-center/AI power demand and electrification but revenue is project-based and sensitive to utility capex cycles.

Eaton.role: Diversified power management company supplying switchgear, UPS, busway and electrical distribution to data centers; strong secular tailwind from AI power demand but earnings remain tied to broader industrial/construction capex cycles.

nVent Electric.role: Electrical connection and protection firm whose liquid-cooling and enclosure products ride data-center buildout, but only a portion of revenue is AI-relevant and demand is tied to cyclical construction capex.

Emerson Electric.role: Diversified industrial automation and process-control supplier benefiting indirectly from data-center electrification and AI capex buildout, but core demand remains cyclical and tied to industrial/energy capital spending.

Johnson Controls.role: Diversified building-systems and HVAC provider whose data center cooling and thermal management products ride AI capex buildout; sits in AI-infra as a quality mid with partial but cyclical exposure to discretionary data center construction.

Trane Technologies.role: Diversified climate/HVAC leader whose thermal-management and data center cooling systems ride AI buildout demand, but the AI-relevant slice is a modest fraction of a cyclical, capex-linked industrial franchise.

Schneider via nVent peer - Hubbell.role: Maker of utility and electrical T&D products benefiting from grid modernization and electrification; sits in defensive given steady demand but moderate cyclicality tied to utility and construction capex.

Vertiv peer - Advanced Energy.role: Advanced Energy makes precision power conversion and control systems for semiconductor equipment, data centers, and industrial markets; it sits in AI-infra with moderate scores because data-center power is a real growth vector but its revenue is heavily tied to cyclical semi-cap and industrial deman

Onsemi peer - Wolfspeed skip - Cree n/a.role: Amkor is a leading outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider gaining from advanced packaging demand, but its commoditized, capital-intensive, cyclical model and thin margins place it as a mid-quality AI-infra enabler with modest moat.

CommScope.role: CommScope supplies fiber, cabling, and connectivity infrastructure for data centers and networks; it's a cyclical, debt-laden hardware vendor with modest AI-driven tailwinds but fragmented competition and leverage risk, placing it in AI-infra with elevated cyclicality.

Corning.role: Diversified materials maker whose Optical Communications segment supplies fiber and connectivity for AI datacenters; strong moat in specialty glass but demand tied to hyperscaler capex cycles, so it sits as quality AI-infra with moderate cyclicality.

InterDigital.role: InterDigital is a patent-licensing firm monetizing a deep wireless (5G/6G), video, and AI-adjacent IP portfolio through recurring royalty agreements; its lumpy-but-sticky licensing revenue and defensive cash flows place it in defensive tech, though the 'Wireless AI' theme is more aspirational extens

Teradyne peer - Cognex.role: Cognex is a leader in machine vision systems and software for factory automation and logistics; it sits in AI-infra given its vision-AI edge, but revenue is tied to cyclical manufacturing/automotive/consumer-electronics capex, capping growth and earnings durability.
